topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: The space where the tree stood is now just an empty patch of dirt, the soil still disturbed from where its roots once held firm. I remember the day I planted it, a tiny sapling no taller than my knee. I can almost feel the rough bark under my fingers, the way the leaves tickled my hand as I watered it. It’s strange how a spot can suddenly seem so barren, so... bare. I replay the memories, the laughter, the quiet moments of just being, under its branches. Now, I find myself standing here, looking at the nothingness, wondering where the time went and why the tree couldn’t stay a little longer.
